review_candidates.title: Senior/Principal RAN Digital Twin & AI Simulation Engineer
review_candidates.description: Parallel Wireless is a U.S.-based pioneer in Open RAN innovation, transforming how mobile networks are built, optimized, and powered. Through our GreenRAN™ portfolio, we help operators deliver secure, energy-efficient, automated, and flexible connectivity across 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G, and the path toward 6G. Our software-centric, hardware-agnostic approach brings intelligence into the RAN while helping customers reduce complexity and total cost of ownership. Parallel Wireless is looking for a hands-on wireless systems engineer to lead the development of a multi-RAT digital twin for our Open RAN solution. The digital twin will execute production RAN software-beginning with scheduler and MAC behavior-in a closed loop with PHY, channel, UE, traffic, and network models. It will allow engineering teams to design, evaluate, and compare features for LTE, 5G NR, and 2G without requiring a dedicated physical radio setup for every development cycle. This is a senior individual-contributor role at the intersection of wireless systems, simulation, production software, and AI/ML. You will evolve an existing LTE end-to-end simulator into a scalable engineering platform for feature development, regression testing, performance optimization, and evidence-based pre-validation. Initial use cases include MAC scheduler and link-adaptation improvements, power control, mobility and interference scenarios, and neural-network-assisted channel estimation. The successful candidate will understand that a useful digital twin must be both fast and trustworthy. You will define multiple fidelity levels-from rapid surrogate models to full PHY processing-and establish repeatable methods for calibrating the twin against lab or field reference data. The goal is to reduce dependence on continuous lab access while maintaining clear, measurable confidence in the simulation results. What you will do: Own the technical architecture and roadmap for a modular, multi-RAT RAN digital twin covering LTE, 5G NR. Integrate production MAC and scheduler software into deterministic, per-TTI/slot closed-loop simulations through stable and maintainable interfaces. Model the interaction among scheduler decisions, PHY processing, propagation channels, UE behavior, traffic, interference, mobility, HARQ, link adaptation, and power control. Extend the current LTE simulation capability and define reusable abstractions that support additional 5G NR and 2G stacks without duplicating the platform. Design a fidelity ladder that combines high-fidelity PHY execution with faster calibrated models or lookup/surrogate backends, selecting the least expensive model that is valid for each engineering question. Develop and evaluate AI/ML-based RAN capabilities, including neural channel estimation, learned link adaptation or scheduling policies, and ML-based PHY or channel surrogates. Build representative datasets and experiment pipelines; establish conventional algorithmic baselines; measure accuracy, robustness, generalization, latency, and compute cost before recommending integration into production software. Create reproducible A/B experiments across software builds and algorithm versions, using defined scenarios, seeds, configurations, and KPIs such as throughput, BLER/ACK-NACK behaviour, MCS, resource-block allocation, SINR, transmit power, latency, and fairness. Establish simulation verification and validation practices: matched sim-vs-lab scenarios, calibration rules, lab-repeatability baselines, divergence analysis, model-version tracking, and evidence reports. Prevent overfitting the twin to a single setup by separating universal model parameters, setup-specific calibration, and the production algorithms under test. Build automated unit, component, end-to-end, regression, and performance tests and integrate them into CI/CD workflows. Improve simulation speed, scale, observability, and usability so that stack, PHY, test, and AI engineers can run repeatable experiments independently. Debug discrepancies across C/C++, Python, MATLAB, PHY models, production stack behaviour, configuration, and reference measurements. Document model assumptions, limitations, supported operating regions, calibration provenance, and the validity of every simulation or ML backend. Work closely with RAN stack, PHY, system architecture, AI/ML, automation, and lab-validation teams to convert product questions into measurable simulation campaigns. What you bring: BSc or MSc in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with substantial relevant industry experience. Typically, 7+ years of hands-on experience in communication systems, system development, integration, or simulation. Experience with RAN, modem/PHY, or wireless systems is an advantage. Demonstrated experience building or validating link-level, system-level, or hardware-in-the-loop simulations and explaining where a model is-and is not-valid. Strong programming skills in C or C++ and Python, including the ability to integrate production native code with simulation and analysis tooling. Practical experience with scientific computing and data analysis using tools such as NumPy, SciPy, pandas, and visualization frameworks. Sound experimental and statistical judgment: reproducibility, baselines, error analysis, uncertainty, calibration, controlled comparisons, and avoidance of data leakage or curve fitting. Experience working in Linux development environments with Git, automated testing, containers, and CI/CD. Ability to lead a technically ambiguous initiative, make architecture decisions, and communicate clearly across research, product, development, and validation teams. Nice to have: A PhD in wireless communications, signal processing or a related area. Hands-on experience developing or evaluating machine-learning models for communications, signal processing, time-series data, or related domains using PyTorch, TensorFlow, or an equivalent framework. Knowledge of LTE and/or 5G NR L1/L2 behavior, including MAC scheduling, link adaptation, HARQ, CQI/SINR feedback, resource allocation, and uplink power control. Knowledge of digital communications and signal processing, including areas such as channel estimation, equalization, coding/modulation, MIMO, propagation and fading models. Extend the current LTE simulation capability and define reusable abstractions that support additional 5G NR and 2G stacks without duplicating the platform. Experience with MATLAB and Communications/LTE/5G toolboxes or equivalent PHY simulation environments. Direct experience with production eNodeB/gNodeB software, commercial modem stacks, or Open RAN products. Knowledge of 3GPP LTE, NR, and/or GERAN specifications and experience translating standards into executable models and test scenarios. Experience with scheduler algorithms such as proportional fair, round robin, maximum C/I, QoS-aware scheduling, or reinforcement-learning-based resource allocation. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Join a global team of 550+ professionals building infrastructure and software that supports the entire digital ecosystem. We are currently looking for an Infrastructure Project Manager, who will independently run projects that deploy and change Gcore infrastructure - from intake through hand-over to operations and formal closure. This is not a role for learning the basics: we expect someone who already runs projects end-to-end, makes operational decisions without constant oversight, and resolves priority and resource conflicts on their own. Projects are initiated by internal product teams (CDN, Cloud, Edge AI, DDoS) or by Technical Support on behalf of external customers. At this level, the PM owns more than Jira tracking: the quality of the plan, realistic timelines, a sound budget estimate, risk management, and coordination of several parallel work streams: architects, procurement, logistics, data centre engineers, and operations teams. We expect a PM to take on a technically and organisationally complex project - a large deployment at a new site, or a multi-vendor integration, and deliver it with minimal involvement from their manager, while proactively communicating status and risks. Projects you will run: PoP build-outs and colocation - new sites, expansion of existing ones, racks and cage space in third-party data centers. Server and network hardware deployments for internal product demand and for external customers (dedicated hardware, managed connectivity). Capacity expansion, hardware refresh, and decommissioning. Connectivity and interconnection procurement - IP transit, cross-connects, dark fiber, wavelengths, leased lines, in coordination with the Peering team. Migrations and relocations of physical equipment between sites. What You'll Do: End-to-end project ownership Setting the project up in Jira ( GI master ticket), breaking it down into tasks, and building a realistic schedule that accounts for dependencies. Identifying the critical path and key risks at kick-off - not waiting for your manager to do it for you. Orchestrating linked tasks across counterpart teams' Jira projects: IDS (architecture), PRO (procurement), DCI (on-site installation), HDWR (repair and replacement). Knowing where the work physically lives, and reporting on the active linked tickets, not just the master ticket. Making operational decisions inside the project yourself. Escalating only what sits outside your authority: budget, priorities between projects, conflicts with other departments. Budget estimation and approvals Initiating cost estimation at the Initiation stage: breakdown by NRC / MRC and by component (colocation, leased lines, hardware, small parts), benchmarked against comparable past projects and reference cost tables. Driving the project through the approval chain, tracking approval turnaround, and handling objections. Reconciling budget plan versus actuals at project closure. Technical design and architecture Briefing the Infrastructure Architects team (RFS / HLD / SDD) and contributing substantively to discussions on BoM, rack layout, power, and network. Being able to tell a realistic technical plan from an unrealistic one, and to ask architects the right clarifying questions. Procurement, vendors, and contractors Briefing the Procurement team (what to buy, by when, for which project) and tracking execution. Vendor negotiations are run by Procurement. Monitoring request and PO statuses, and escalating early when timelines are at risk. Agreeing responsibility boundaries (RACI) between the project, Procurement, and the vendor where this affects the plan. Logistics and delivery to site Briefing the Logistics team (what needs to go where, and by when) and tracking execution. Shipping, customs, warehousing, and delivery to the data center are run by the Logistics team. Tracking ETAs and escalating early when delivery is at risk of slipping. On-site installation Briefing the DCIM team on equipment installation: agreeing installation windows, tracking timelines and quality of execution. Handling discrepancies found at acceptance: missing equipment, equipment routed to stock, equipment routed to repair. Hand-over to operations Running the hand-over to the Server Operations and Network Operations teams. These teams sit outside the Infrastructure Department, so the hand-over requires explicit agreements on content, quality, and timing: documentation, configurations, monitoring on-boarding. Organizing and confirming acceptance testing, formally closing the project (sign-off), and capturing lessons learned. Risk and stakeholder management Identifying risks proactively, before they become problems, and proposing options rather than only reporting the issue. Communicating regularly and substantively with stakeholders at different levels: product teams, vendors, operations teams, leadership. Managing scope changes: assessing impact on timeline and budget, getting agreement, recording it in Jira. Flow and metrics (Kanban) The team operates as a Kanban system: no sprints, with WIP limits and flow metrics. Jira statuses are the source of truth for all reporting, so status hygiene is part of the job rather than a nice-to-have: tickets move when work actually starts and finishes, not at the end of the week and not retroactively. Understanding the difference between Customer Lead Time (what the requester experiences) and System Lead Time (what the team controls), working to the target P85 for your components, and acting on your own Aging WIP before your manager has to point it out. Process improvement Contributing to better processes and templates inside IPM: RACI, readiness checklists, documentation standards, status entry and exit criteria. What We're Looking For: Minimum 2 years in project management in infrastructure, data centres, telecom, or IT operations. Readiness to run a project without step-by-step support is a hard requirement. Solid understanding of server and network hardware and how a data center works : racks, PDUs, power and cooling, basic network topology (switches, cross-connects, IP addressing) — at a level sufficient for a substantive conversation with architects and engineers, not just to recognize the terminology. Experience with Jira (or an equivalent tracker) at project-administration level: linking tasks across projects, working with workflows and fields, not only changing statuses. A high degree of personal ownership and autonomy. There is no micromanagement in this team: you keep your projects under control, surface risks yourself, and keep the team informed on substance without being asked. Ability to work with ambiguity and to run several projects in parallel. English at B2 or above - enough for correspondence and negotiation with international partners and vendors. Documentation is written in English. Strong communication skills: able to convey complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences. Nice to have: Experience with flow-based management (Kanban) and with Lead Time, Throughput, and WIP metrics. Experience in multi-vendor / multi-partner projects with a formal RACI. Experience with budget estimation for infrastructure projects (NRC / MRC, colocation, leased lines). Project management certification (PMP, Kanban Management Professional, or similar). Experience working in a distributed international team. Benefits: At Gcore, we want you to do your best work and enjoy the journey. review_candidates.title: Regional SDR Director
review_candidates.description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder led, profitable and growing. We are expanding our sales and field engineering teams globally, including our sales development representative (SDR) teams. Our SDRs and BDRs are typically outstanding graduates from STEM fields who would like to join the software industry and are starting their sales career at Canonical. We are hiring Regional SDR Directors to run our inbound and outbound teams across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. Our goal is not only to manage inbound leads for a global tech company, but also to develop outstanding sales professionals with high integrity, high empathy and a rigorous work ethic. Our sales development organisation is therefore also a sales academy, and as such, we are looking for Regional SDR & BDR Directors who take a strong interest in the development of skills and the establishment of culture across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. You will enjoy this role if you are organised, persistent, analytical, hard-working, and care to ensure that smart and ambitious people learn and develop the skills they need to represent you and the company in outstandingly well over the course of their career, both while they are on your team, and as they move onward to more senior sales and alliances positions. You should be determined to grow your own skills as well as those of your team, and enjoy learning about new technologies. Canonical is fortunate to represent the vast wave of open source innovation, which means it has a large and rapidly growing range of solutions it can deliver to customers, and ample opportunity for all of us to learn about new kinds of tech, or specialise in fields we enjoy the most. You should also be open to innovation, and experiment with new outbound approaches to adapt to changes in the market. In this role your primary objective is to direct regional SDR & BDR managers and teams across AMER, EMEA, and APAC, and maintain a multi-million dollar pipeline. We value Excellent academic results at school and university Bachelor’s or equivalent degree in Business or STEM Knowledge and passion for business development, sales and technology Track record of bringing exceptional outbound sales development results Commitment to continuous learning and improvement - curious, flexible, scientific Creative problem solving and cross team collaboration Leadership experience of one form or another Able to use data to drive team activities and continuous improvement Multi-regional strategic vision tailored to AMER, EMEA, and APAC market dynamics Track record of recruiting, mentoring, and developing SDR Team Managers (leading leaders) Cross-functional alignment with Regional Sales VPs, Marketing, and Field Engineering Expertise in leveraging modern sales tech stacks and CRM analytics for predictable pipeline forecasting Scalable talent pipeline management to feed senior sales and alliances positions across all three regions Experience driving accountability and culture across asynchronous, remote-first global teams Over the last few years, this team has trained dozens of talented tech sales professionals who now work at Canonical and across the industry. Meet some of the SDRs who have graduated from our tech sales academy. What We Offer You We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Employee Assistance Programme Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical is an equal opportunity employer We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
